subject: Vendor swap analysis and price match request - BrightLayer
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightlayer.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightLayer: price parity ask + migration economics

Hi Sean,

Quick intro — I run procurement for BrightLayer. We're evaluating a potential move from our current vendor, NimbusAI, to Redwood. Nimbus has offered a time-limited 20% list discount plus 3 months of waived overage fees to lock in our renewal.

Before we set up a commercial deep-dive, can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: 1) a price-match for our committed tier, 2) an explicit migration credit structure (amount and trigger), and 3) any constraints around model compatibility that would affect runtime parity?

We're aiming to present a recommendation to our CFO by 11/25. Simple bullets and a quick cost delta table would be most helpful.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Head of Procurement | BrightLayer
procurement@brightlayer.com

---
(Attachment: incumbent-offer-summary.pdf (PDF, 42KB) referenced)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.example
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightlayer.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer: price parity ask + migration economics

Maria — thanks for the note and the timeline. We can absolutely respond with a concrete proposal. High level:

- Price-match: we can match equivalent runtime economics for committed throughput with a 12-month commitment window; we typically layer a modest onboarding credit rather than matching a short-term promotional discount in perpetuity.
- Migration credit: we offer a tiered migration credit tied to committed annual spend (examples below). Credits are usable as service credits over the first 6 months post-go-live.
- Runtime parity: most models and runtimes are compatible; differences come down to quantization and accelerator selection. We'll include an ops checklist for parity risks.

I've looped in Marissa (pricing) and Lauren (legal/commercial) to draft the specifics and a short econ model. Could you share your expected committed spend range and the Nimbus contract term so we can map apples-to-apples?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.example
(Attachment: request-received.txt (plain) )

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightlayer.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer: price parity ask + migration economics — proposal attached

Maria — attaching a short packet that breaks down three options: parity-match (short-term promotional bridge), committed discount with onboarding credit, and a hybrid migration rebate tied to go-live milestones. Highlights:

- Option A (Parity bridge): 20% discount on list for 6 months + 2 months free overage buffer; designed to neutralize Nimbus' promotional window.
- Option B (Commit + Credit): 10% recurring discount for 12 months + $150k migration credit applied across months 0–6; requires 12-month committed ARR of $1.2M+.
- Option C (Hybrid): 8% recurring discount + $200k milestone-based rebate (paid after successful scale verification).

We also include an operations handshake checklist and an initial compatibility matrix (see redwood-vs-nimbus-econ-matrix.xlsx). A few quick notes on constraints: GPU packing differences may create a 3–7% latency variance on peak short tails until we optimize kernels — we can target parity within the first 30 days with a small co-optimization runway.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call to walk the packet and agree on which option to model. I'm available 11/18 between 10–1 PT.

Attachments:
- redwood-vs-nimbus-econ-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 58KB)
- migration-credit-term-sheet.pdf (PDF, 32KB)
- deployment-handshake-checklist.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@brightlayer.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 07:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer: price parity ask + migration economics — proposal attached

Marissa — thanks for the packet; the level of detail helps. Quick reactions from procurement and the engineering lead:

- Procurement prefers Option B (Commit + Credit) if you can bring the APR discount to 12% and make at least $100k of the migration credit payable upon a signed SOW rather than delayed milestone triggers. Our CFO is sensitive to the net present value of delayed rebates.
- Engineering flagged the 3–7% latency variance; they'd like a written SLA addendum for the first 60 days clarifying remediation steps and fallback to our current vendor if parity targets aren't met.

We can do a 30-minute call 11/18 at 11:30 PT. If you can send a slim redlineable term summary before that call, we can expedite approval.

Best,
Maria
